html:
Ravi Shankar was a sitar player and composer who made Indian classical music known around the world.

He was born in 1920 in Varanasi to a Bengali family. At ten he went to Paris with the dance company of his brother Uday and toured Europe and America as a dancer. At eighteen he gave it up. He spent seven years in the small town of Maihar as a pupil of the stern master Allauddin Khan, practising up to fourteen hours a day.

By the 1950s he was a leading player in India. He directed music for All India Radio and wrote the score for Pather Panchali and the other films of Satyajit Ray's Apu trilogy. From 1956 he toured the West, explaining each raga to the audience before he played.

In 1966 George Harrison of the Beatles became his pupil, and the sitar was suddenly heard in pop music everywhere. Shankar played at the Monterey and Woodstock festivals, though he disliked the drugs and the noise. In 1971 he and Harrison staged the Concert for Bangladesh in New York for the refugees of the war, the first large charity rock concert.

He recorded with the violinist Yehudi Menuhin and wrote concertos for sitar and orchestra. His daughters Anoushka Shankar and Norah Jones are both musicians.
sum: Ravi Shankar was a sitar player and composer who made Indian classical music known around the world.
